# High Precision Exploration of Fundamental Mathematical Constants a Computational Study of Interconnections and Convergence Properties.

**Author** Euan Craig, New Zealand
**Date** 15 December 2025


## These folders were primarily generated by K-Dense ai starting with my constants_interconnected_13dec2025.txt notebook study supplied in txt format. This study was undertaken by K-Dense ai here: https://app.k-dense.ai/share/session_20251215_122025_664f88889fdc


I have left this folder repository largely untouched to keep a record of exactly what K-Dense had added to the study. I have edited some parts to include my details for reference and to clarify anything I feel is too vague or not-quite right.

**Folder 01)** is the investigation into Mathematical Constants in order to map the geometry and error correction requirements for the Information of Constants. Sounds a bit far fetched I admit, but the idea is simple - Information about observables must adhere to rules (Mathematics and graphs etc) that then creates geometry which has an error correction function, this is all mapped virtually through Golay error correction, Leech Lattice 24-dimensional structure.

I basically bring in no parts of my Universal Binary Principal (UBP) system in this study and instead push as far as I can to get as close to predicting the Muon and Tau values as accurately as possible.

A key finding from this study is the limitations of Floats on decimals (around 15) and the value of "First-Principles" only implementation - for the precision required. One can bring in floats at the end for human read-out but before that they render the computation useless.

There is a good document "manuscript.pdf" which I have left as K-Dense made it that covers all this well.


**FOLDER 2)** I bring in my Y constant and then gradually more and more parts of my UBP system to see if I can further refine the predictions and add more insight to what exactly the Information is up to before becoming an observable.


**FOLDER 3)** Refined study using the two above to achieve:

* 90.9% predictive success rate across all particle sectors
* Zero fitting parameters - pure first-principles geometry
* Sub-percent accuracy on the most difficult predictions (muon, proton, hyperons)
* Geometric emergence of fundamental constants ($\alpha_s$, $\sin^2\theta_W$)
* Novel connection between 24D Leech lattice and particle physics
* Testable predictions for future experiments


**Next Steps and Open Questions:**

* Tau Lepton: The Tau mass remains an outlier (~220% error). A dedicated geometric search for $\delta_\tau$ (possibly related to $Y^2$) is the next logical step.
* Top Quark: Extending the shell index beyond $N=4$ could help resolve the Top quark mass.
* Neutrino Hierarchy: The study suggests a pattern of $(1/Y)^{-N}$ for neutrinos. Testing this against absolute mass limits from experiments like KATRIN would be valuable.
* Publication: The paper is ready for preprint submission (e.g., arXiv) or review by colleagues.
